question: A 1-month-old male newborn is brought to the physician because of poor feeding, a hoarse cry, and lethargy for 1 week. The boy was born in Mozambique, from where he and his parents emigrated 2 weeks ago. He is at the 95th percentile for head circumference, 50th percentile for length, and 70th percentile for weight. Physical examination shows scleral icterus, an enlarged tongue, and generalized hypotonia. The abdomen is distended and there is a reducible, soft protruding mass at the umbilicus. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Umbilical hernia -> Enlarged tongue -> Generalized hypotonia -> 80% CHAIN: Scleral icterus -> Biliary atresia -> Abdominal distension -> 70% CHAIN: Hoarse cry -> Thyroid dysgenesis -> Poor feeding -> 60% CHAIN: Emigration from Mozambique -> Congenital toxoplasmosis -> Lethargy -> 50% CHAIN: High head circumference percentile -> Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome -> Soft protruding mass at umbilicus -> 80%
analysis: The constellation of symptoms including poor feeding, hoarse cry, lethargy, enlarged tongue, hypotonia, scleral icterus, and a soft protruding mass at the umbilicus in a 1-month-old male newborn with the described growth parameters is highly suggestive of congenital hypothyroidism. The most likely cause among the given options is thyroid dysgenesis.
